title: Culture, Ethics and Why Conduct Matters
summary: What culture and conduct mean in a regulated firm, why supervisors care about them, and how everyday behaviour shapes outcomes for customers and markets.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: What culture and conduct mean in a regulated firm, why supervisors care about them, and how everyday behaviour shapes outcomes for customers and markets.
Learning Objectives: Explain the link between culture, conduct and customer and market outcomes
Recognise the signs of healthy and unhealthy cultures
Describe what supervisors and customers expect of firms and their staff
Syllabus: Conduct risk in plain terms: how harm happens
Culture: tone from the top, the middle and within teams
Lessons from major conduct failures across the industry
Seeing your firm the way a supervisor does
Intended Audience: All staff in regulated firms, from new joiners to experienced colleagues, as induction or annual refresher training
Customer-facing, product, marketing, operations, technology and support staff whose work affects customer outcomes
Team leaders and managers who set the tone for conduct and respond when concerns are raised
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior knowledge of regulation is required. Some experience of working with customers is helpful but not essential.
Core Reading: FSB (2018), Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors
G20/OECD (2022), High-Level Principles on Financial Consumer Protection
FSB (2014), Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture: A Framework for Assessing Risk Culture
ISO (2021), ISO 37002:2021 Whistleblowing Management Systems – Guidelines
